new_blocker_S6.root_cause_read_from_the_running_code: core/llm/jobs.py's _re_ask (jobs.py:554-565) builds the correction message by substituting the rejection's own error strings into `manifest.rejection_template` - the SAME template for every rejection reason section_authoring can raise. prompts/section_authoring.yaml's rejection_template (lines 13-16) is written entirely for the identifier/citation defect class ('cite only accepted fact IDs', 'a stray identifier that names no accepted fact', 'the citation belongs only in fact_ids') - it says nothing about a _FORBIDDEN marker (a command, a URL, Markdown, HTML). A rejection whose actual cause is 'text contains a command' therefore receives correction guidance that does not mention commands, markers, or rephrasing at all; the model's one re-ask has no signal for what to change and reproduces the same sentence.
new_blocker_S6.why_this_looks_like_pgpy_04s_own_shape_o: PGPY-04/item 111 closed an identical-shaped gap for presentation_planning: a rejection message alone, with no actionable correction, cost a wasted re-ask. There the fix was a deterministic server-side splice because item 95's hint already named real candidate facts. Here there is no equivalent hint to splice from - the defect is not a missing citation but a literal forbidden substring the model chose to write - so the analogous fix is a better CORRECTION, not a deterministic recovery: the rejection_template (or a marker-aware variant of it) needs to name the offending fragment and instruct the model to describe the requirement in prose without repeating the literal command (the renderer already prints install_command facts as its own code block in the Installation section, so restating the command in scope_limitations is always redundant by construction, never merely miswritten).

proposal.proposed_shape: Not prescribed here (owner's choice, per the items 95/102/103 precedent of narrow, evidence-fitted widenings): (a) branch the correction message on the rejection's own shape - when the failing reason names a _FORBIDDEN marker rather than a stray identifier, append a sentence naming the exact offending fragment and stating that the renderer already prints commands/links/markup itself, so the unit must describe the requirement in plain prose with no literal command, URL, or markup; or (b) a deterministic last-resort recover= for section_authoring, symmetrical to item 111's, that strips only the offending literal substring from the unit's text (never inventing replacement prose, since a command's surrounding sentence may itself need rewriting) and re-validates through the real unit_checks before accepting - weaker than the generic case because there is no guarantee stripping the fragment leaves grammatical prose, so (a) is likely the safer first attempt.
proposal.explicitly_not_proposed: No relaxation of the _FORBIDDEN table or unit_checks' marker rule itself - the check is correct: the renderer already owns the Installation section's command block, and restating it in scope_limitations prose is exactly the duplication section 6 rule 13/authoring.py's own docstring (lines 698-705) already forbids.
